settings.title: Overview of the Automatic Quadruple-Outlet Gas Filling Machine
settings.text:
Argon is a noble gas that is odorless, colorless, and non-flammable. Because it does not readily undergo chemical reactions, it is safely used in the cavity between two glass panes. If the glass breaks and the gas leaks into a building, it poses no harm to occupants.
Argon must be introduced into the cavity using specialized equipment to ensure effective insulation against cold air and noise.
In recent years, advanced manufacturers have developed quadruple-outlet gas filling machines to simplify the work of glass industry professionals and enable precise gas filling.
Among the various four-outlet machines on the market, the automatic model is a leading option because it can fill four glass units with argon simultaneously.
The machine is lightweight and has standard dimensions, allowing a single operator to move it easily.

settings.title: Why Gas Filling Is Used in Double-Glazed Glass Production
settings.text:
Modern design increasingly emphasizes attractive finishes. Double-glazed glass allows decorative profiles to be installed in grids or custom patterns.
Filling the cavity between the panes with argon supports energy savings as well as the product's aesthetic applications.
Because properly manufactured double-glazed units have a low heat-transfer coefficient, heat transfer is reduced, helping maintain indoor heating and cooling.
Depending on the gap between the panes, the gas used, and glass thickness, energy consumption can be reduced by up to approximately 40%, while also improving noise insulation.
Argon filling using dedicated equipment is important for two main reasons:

Sound Insulation

Noise pollution is widespread and can adversely affect people's well-being. This type of glass helps reduce external noise entering a building and creates a quieter indoor environment.

Thermal Insulation

This glass helps retain indoor heat in cold weather and keep interiors cooler in hot weather, making it useful in both summer and winter.

settings.title: Features of the Quadruple-Outlet Gas Filling Machine
settings.text:
Among the machines used to fill the cavity between double-glazed panes, the automatic quadruple-outlet gas filling machine is particularly valued by industrial manufacturers.
It fills four glass units with gas simultaneously, easily and at high speed.
Its distinctive features include:
Simultaneous filling of four glass units with different dimensions and thicknesses
Smart programs that calculate the required gas filling according to glass dimensions and thickness
Compatible with double-glazing production methods, including warm-edge spacers, polysulfide, and hot-melt systems
Equipped with a PLC touchscreen and physical control buttons
An automatic shut-off sensor that stops the machine when filling is complete if no operator is present
